conclusion: No alphabetical or duplicate-home ownership defect explains any of the 151 actual native errors. All 148 undeclared-prerequisite diagnostics have exact actual direct selected dependency causes whose supplier IDs each occur on one physical library page. Three B-leaf diagnostics also refer to actual singly homed B-page suppliers. Preserve these failures for root reconciliation; no mechanical waiver or ownership-selection code patch is justified by this evidence.
mechanical_authority_findings: validate-plan current manifest overlay retains unique selected ownership and item inventories. The canonical plan contains no multiply declared item IDs in this observed snapshot.

For external item/page graph context, pageSucc prefers canonical pageOfItem and only falls back to the first physical library home. The potentially arbitrary fallback exists, but none of the actual 148 undeclared roots is multiply placed.

The only multiply physically placed suppliers among selected direct item dependencies are def-ordered-field and def-complete-ordered-field, on construction-of-r-via-cauchy-sequences and foundations-of-the-real-numbers. These explain none of the native errors.

content-policy uses canonical plan item homes for same-page reuse; audit-frontier retains an exact canonical companion home when duplicated across a known pair. Neither authorizes inventing a home for a uniquely placed general-purpose helper.

The SCHEMA first-home convention and existing tests preserve leaf, current manifest, actual external supplier dependency, missing prerequisite and closure checks. No condition was weakened or skipped.
